text:
alex: Heads up — after merging runtime change abc123 I see a consistent ~10% p99 regression on Batcher-heavy RTX jobs. Started around 3901228000 so probably from that roll. Captured an nsys and a perfetto trace: gs://redwood-perf/3901234567/nsys.qdrep and https://perfetto.dev/trace/3901234567

maria: Ugh. Any obvious hotspot? kernel selector flip? :eyes:

alex: Looking like kernel selection + increased memcopy windows. In the timeline the selector picks a different conv kernel for mid-sized sequences, then we get a burst of memcopies and KV cache eviction chatter. Screenshot: https://internal-imgs/3901234567/kerneltl.png

chen: Can you paste the short nvprof/nsys command you used? I'll try a local repro.

alex: Ran this on a repro harness (shortened):
```
nsys profile -o run_3901234567 --trace=cuda,nvtx -t cuda,osrt --sample=none
python -m runtime.repro --model t5-large --seq 1024 --batch 8 --warmup 20 --iter 200
```
Capture has two sections: pre-merge (baseline) and post-merge (spike) separated by a `roll` nvtx mark.

jamal: Quick grep of the nsys CSV shows a jump in `cudaMemcpyAsync` time and an extra 12ms in kernel_selection() for op_conv_fp16 -> op_conv_generic path. Maybe the heuristic added a fallback check.

alex: Here's a tiny log snippet from the trace (post-merge):
```
[3901234567.121] kernel_selection: chose op_conv_generic (est 18.2ms) over op_conv_int8 (est 7.6ms) -- cost_miss 10.6
[3901234567.133] cudaMemcpyAsync HtoD 14.1ms
[3901234567.147] kv_cache: evict shard-3, prefix_hit_drop=0.72->0.31
```

maria: kv hit drop is suspect. If selector changes kernel shape it can alter temp memory layout and bump eviction. Could be an allocator alignment regression.

chen: I'll bisect the commit range. Suggest `git bisect run` with the repro harness. Range: abc000..abc123. I'll kick it off and post the commit that flips it.

perf-bot: [smoke] 3901234567 — perf regression detected in job `batcher-p99` (+9.7% p99). Regression window: 3901227000..3901234000. Linked traces: gs://redwood-perf/3901234567/nsys.qdrep

jamal: If bisect points to the selector heuristic commit we should add a unit test exercising medium-seq conv choices and a perf test to prevent regressing kernel cost estimates.

alex: Agreed. For repro notes: the spike reproduces with sequence mix ~40% long, 60% mid. Workload generator: `tools/workload_gen --mix 40:60 --batch 8 --seq-mid 512 --seq-long 2048`. Also try toggling `RUNTIME_KERNEL_COST_OVERRIDES=1` to see if fallback goes away.

chen: Started bisect job — will report the first bad commit here. ETA ~15m.

maria: Thanks. If it pins to selector I can prototype a cheap cache-friendly tie-breaker (prefer kernels with contiguous scratch if cost delta < 5ms).

alex: Nice. One more ask: when you run the nsys diff, please use `nsys stats --report=summary` and attach the CSV. It makes comparing kernel-level deltas easier.

perf-bot: [update] bisect job queued (id: 6732). Will post results to thread when finished. :white_check_mark:
